commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Skip MoE-LoRA shrink/expand when no LoRA is active
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Skip the MoE-LoRA shrink/expand launches when there are no active LoRAs, fixing a segmentation fault on XPU in `test_fused_moe_lora_kernel_zero_grid_no_crash[two_kernel]` ([Intel CI build 16155](https://buildkite.com/vllm/intel-ci/builds/16155#01a19356-b9b6-4244-a603-173c195758e5)). Follow-up to #64653.

## Claims

- `_fused_moe_lora_shrink` / `_fused_moe_lora_expand` no longer launch a Triton grid with a zero dimension when `num_active_loras == 0`.
- The output is left unchanged in that case, as the existing test asserts.

## Validation

- Before: `pytest tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py -k zero_grid_no_crash` on XPU (Arc Pro B60, torch 2.14) -> `Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault`.
- After: `pytest tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py` on XPU -> 463 passed.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check`: passed.

commits.pr_title: [Kernel] Enable CuteDSL GDN prefill on SM110
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Lets the opt-in CuteDSL GDN prefill backend (`--gdn-prefill-backend cutedsl`) run on SM110 (Jetson Thor), and fixes its kernel launch on GPUs with fewer SMs than value heads. Related: #63284 rewrites the same selector function, so whichever PR merges second will need a small rebase. #62149 is a separate Thor GDN warmup crash that this PR does not fix.

## Claims

- `--gdn-prefill-backend cutedsl` now runs on SM110. Before, the selector fell back to Triton/FLA.
- On GPUs with fewer SMs than value heads, the CuteDSL kernels failed to launch with `CUDA_LAUNCH_INVALID_CONFIG`. Thor has 20 SMs and Qwen3.8-27B has 48 value heads. The kernels now launch at least one CTA per head.
- On Thor with `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`, cutedsl lowers TTFT on 16k-token prompts by about 6% compared with triton. GSM8K is within error.
- `auto` makes the same choice as before on every platform. On SM10x, the larger grid size only takes effect for models with more than 148 value heads.

## Validation

Jetson AGX Thor (SM110, 20 SMs), CUDA 13.2, `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` (BF16, `head_k_dim=128`, 48 value heads).

**Kernel test** (`tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_prefill_cutedsl.py`):

| | Result |
|---|---|
| Without the `num_sms` fix | 6 failed, 7 passed: every `num_v_heads=160` case raises `CUDA_LAUNCH_INVALID_CONFIG` in `kkt_inv_uw_cutedsl` |
| With the fix | 13 passed |

**End to end**, `--gdn-prefill-backend triton` vs `cutedsl` (startup logs confirm the selected kernel):

| Backend | GSM8K strict | GSM8K flexible | Mean TTFT (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | P90 TTFT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| triton | 0.7058 | 0.7339 | 16573.6 ± 8.9 | 16563.6 ± 11.8 | 16634.4 ± 14.0 |
| cutedsl | 0.6990 | 0.7240 | 15555.3 ± 1.0 | 15551.1 ± 1.6 | 15565.8 ± 6.6 |

- GSM8K: full 1319-question set, 5-shot. lm-eval reports a standard error of ±0.012–0.013 per score, so the −0.7 / −1.0 point differences are within noise.
- TTFT: 16k-token random prompts, 1 output token, concurrency 1, 16 prompts per run, 3 runs with seeds 1–3 (mean ± stdev). `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, so each prompt is prefilled in two chunks.
- All 48 benchmark requests succeeded on both backends, and neither server log has errors.

CI has no SM110 runner. The B200 `Kernels` job runs the updated test, and its `num_v_heads=160` case exceeds the B200's 148 SMs, so it covers the grid fix.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
pytest -v tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_prefill_cutedsl.py

vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B --max-num-seqs 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --language-model-only --gdn-prefill-backend {triton,cutedsl}

lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k \
  --model_args model=Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=8,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False

vllm bench serve --model Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 16384 --random-output-len 1 --num-prompts 16 \
  --max-concurrency 1 --seed {1,2,3} --percentile-metrics ttft,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90
```

</details>

## Details

- **Root cause:** `kkt_inv_uw_cutedsl` and `o_cutedsl` launch `grid = (num_sms // Hv, Hv, 1)`. When `num_sms < Hv`, the first grid dimension is 0 and CUDA rejects the launch. Both kernels now clamp the first grid dimension to at least 1 (`cutlass.max(num_sms // Hv, 1)`), which gives one CTA per head and also covers direct callers of the kernels. Both kernels loop over chunks with a stride equal to the grid size (`range(bid, num_global_chunks, grid_x)`), so the grid size doesn't affect results. `kernel_h` uses a `(Hv, N)` grid and isn't affected.
- **Selector:** SM11x with `head_k_dim == 128` and CUDA 13+ now allows CuteDSL. It doesn't allow FlashInfer, so `auto` still resolves to Triton on SM110.
- **Not a duplicate of #63284:** that PR splits "can run" from "preferred" for FlashInfer and CuteDSL, but doesn't add SM110 or touch the kernel grid size. If it merges first, this PR only needs SM110 added to its `can_run_cutedsl` check and its "targets SM100" error text updated.
- **Test gap:** no unit test checks that the selector picks CuteDSL on SM110. CI has no SM110 GPU, and faking the GPU type would need mocks. The startup log line from the Thor run is the evidence instead.
- **Docs:** the `--gdn-prefill-backend` help text now says where `cutedsl` works.
- AI assistance (Claude) was used to write and validate this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and benchmarks above.

---

commits.pr_title: [Attention][DCP] Support DCP on the FlashMLA sparse bf16 KV path
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Enables decode context parallelism (DCP) for `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` with a bf16 KV cache. Until now the bf16 path raised `NotImplementedError` under DCP.

Related: #46514 (DCP for the `fp8_ds_mla` mixed-batch path, which added the bf16 guard), #61285 (`a2a` comm backend for the same backend).

## Claims

- `--kv-cache-dtype bfloat16` with `--decode-context-parallel-size > 1` now runs on `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`. On Hopper, no other sparse MLA backend supports DCP.
- GSM8K accuracy matches DCP1: 0.904 at DCP4 vs 0.894 at DCP1 on GLM-5.3-Flash.
- bf16 is not bound by the fp8 DCP limits (mixed-batch only, head envelope). For example, 32 local heads at DCP4 and 16 at DCP8 are accepted.
- On GLM-5.3-Flash, DCP4 holds 1.40× the KV tokens of DCP1.

## Validation

**Setup.** One GH200 node, 4× GPUs (96 GB, SM90). `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, TP4, `--quantization fp8` (weights only; the KV cache stays bf16).

**Unit tests.** `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k dcp`: 10 passed, 3 of them new.

**GSM8K.** `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 500 questions, 5-shot, greedy, seed 42, CUDA graphs on. Both runs set `sparse_mla_force_mqa`, so prefill rows also take the changed path; otherwise GSM8K prompts (shorter than `index_topk`) would go to dense MHA and only decode would be tested.

| DCP | Accuracy | Invalid | Output tok/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.894 | 0.000 | 833 |
| 4 (`ag_rs`) | 0.904 | 0.000 | 726 |

The difference is within the ~1.3-point standard error at n=500.

**KV-cache capacity.** Same per-rank KV memory budget in each row.

| Mode | DCP1 tokens | DCP4 tokens | Ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| eager | 225,475 | 315,665 | 1.40× |
| CUDA graphs | 216,892 | 302,557 | 1.39× |

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

```bash
# DCP1: drop the three DCP flags on the second line
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 4 --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 4 --dcp-comm-backend ag_rs \
  --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE \
  --attention-config '{"sparse_mla_force_mqa": true}' \
  --quantization fp8 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 --port 8000

python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 \
  --num-questions 500 --num-shots 5 --max-concurrency 64 --seed 42
```

- `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 4`: required by GLM-5.3-Flash's indexer KV compression (`compress_ratio=4`) under DCP.
- `--max-num-seqs 128`: keeps the per-request state blocks within memory for CUDA graph capture.

</details>

## Details

- **Root cause.** Under DCP each rank holds a shard of the KV cache, but the indexer emits global token ids. The bf16 path converted them with `triton_convert_req_index_to_global_index`, which treats every index as local, so it would read slots owned by other ranks. #46514 enabled DCP for fp8 only and added a guard rejecting bf16.
- **Fix.** `_forward_bf16_kv` converts top-k with `triton_filter_and_convert_dcp_index`, as the fp8 path and the sparse MLA base already do. Its compacted output and valid counts map directly onto `flash_mla_sparse_fwd`'s `topk_length`.
- **Empty rows.** For a row where this rank owns none of the selected tokens, `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` returns `lse=+inf` (FlashMLA `tests/ref.py`). Those rows are set to `-inf`, the identity of the cross-rank merge, as the fp8 path does. The output is made contiguous for the combine.
- **Guards.** The bf16 kernel returns the LSE for every token and pads the gathered heads itself, so the builder's mixed-batch and head-envelope checks now apply to fp8 caches only. PCP+DCP with bf16 and HiSparse+DCP are still rejected.
- **Cost.** bf16 KV is ~1.75× the size of `fp8_ds_mla`, so fp8 stays preferable where its DCP path applies. This PR covers the configs it rejects and deployments that need a bf16 cache.
- **Not a duplicate.** Searched open PRs and issues for "DCP FlashMLA sparse bf16" and "DCP sparse bf16 fp8_ds_mla". #54541 touches the same conversion but backports to v0.28.0, which predates #46514's guard.
- **Tests.** `test_bf16_dcp_skips_fp8_guards` covers the builder and `test_bf16_dcp_filters_topk_and_neutralizes_empty_rows` covers the forward path, both in `test_sparse_mla_backends.py`.

---

commits.pr_title: [UMBP][7/10] Add standalone mode backed by a node-local server
commits.pr_body:
This PR is split from the original full PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58568

Add the node-local UMBP server runtime and its endpoint and startup checks.
Share one DRAM pool across engines and DP ranks. vLLM does not start the server, and KV bytes stay on HIP IPC instead of the Unix socket.
Fail closed when the server is unreachable, reject pool-sizing and `dram_*` options, and hold stores while the shared pool is blocked.
Key the shared namespace on the effective model config (dtype, quantization, and `hf_config` after `hf_overrides`), so engines that share a model path but produce different KV never read each other's blocks.
Fail transfers queued behind a blocked store instead of waiting on them forever, and bound shutdown so a stalled server cannot hang worker close or process exit.

Implementation only. Usage is in the Standalone mode section of `docs/features/umbp_store_connector_usage.md`. Tests are in the next PR.

Commit: `e02b5bccd8`. Review slice of [vllm-project/vllm#58568](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58568) for [RFC #57187](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57187). Related upstream draft: [vllm-project/vllm#59275](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59275).

AI assistance was used to draft this description. The submitting human reviews the code.

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode][MRV2] Suffix decoding speculator for Model Runner V2
commits.pr_body:
## Overview `method="suffix"` today needs Arctic Inference, runs on the CPU, forces Model Runner V1 and disables async scheduling. With this PR it runs on Model Runner V2 with a GPU speculator, with async scheduling and without Arctic; V1 keeps using Arctic. This is the "suffix" item in #47172. The speculator builds on `ngram_gpu` (#40704) and borrows from #52097 (thanks @zip95297). Related fix on main: #61509 (adaptive verification's startup profiling was counted as CUDA graph memory). @njhill rebased this onto the speculator config refactor and simplified it: seeded requests are no longer special-cased, and the runner hooks are `BaseSpeculator` methods. ## Claims - `method="suffix"` runs on Model Runner V2: GPU-resident, no host sync on the propose path, async scheduling, no Arctic dependency. V1 is unchanged except for the default `num_speculative_tokens` (below). - Acceptance is on par with Arctic: 1.937 tokens per step vs Arctic's 1.923 (k=8) and 1.948 (k=24) on a 21K-request replay. - With adaptive verification, throughput matches or beats Arctic on V1 at every concurrency for Qwen2.5-7B (offline and online serving) and for Qwen2.5-1.5B from concurrency 64 up; at 1.5B concurrency 8 and 32 Arctic is ahead (below). Without adaptive verification, verifying every slot loses from concurrency 32 up, as with `ngram_gpu`. - GSM8K accuracy matches no speculation. - `num_speculative_tokens` now defaults to 8 for suffix decoding (was `suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth`, 24), because V2 verifies every slot. ## Validation The results below were measured before @njhill's rebase and simplification. That change only affects requests with an explicit `seed`, and none of these benchmarks send per-request seeds, so they still apply. #61509 has since merged, so the "with #61509" figures are what adaptive verification gets on current main. **Tests** ```bash pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_suffix_speculator.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py # 49 passed pytest tests/test_config.py -k "speculative or suffix or heterogeneous or model_runner" # 68 passed pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_ngram_gpu.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_custom_speculator.py # 58 passed pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/ngram_suffix/test_ngram_suffix.py -k suffix # 3 passed ``` The e2e tests ran with the CI model's weights (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) on one L4, before the simplification (which doesn't touch greedy decoding): - The V2 GSM8K correctness test passes (76.3%). At the old default k=24 it ran out of memory: V2 profiles one logits row per request, while every step computes 1 + k. - The V2 cross-request test gives 0.74 → 4.47 accepted tokens per draft on the repeated pass. With Qwen2.5-1.5B it's 1.32 → 5.12, and 1.28 → 1.28 with the corpus off, which the test's `second > 2 * first` check rejects. - The Arctic acceptance test (V1) passes. **Runtime checks** - **No new host syncs:** `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` with and without adaptive verification, including ingestion. - **TP=2:** corpus, index, statistics and drafts are identical on both ranks after 312 requests, with and without adaptive verification, on the default ring and on a 2,048-token ring where bursts of up to 48 finished requests wrap over themselves. **Acceptance.** Replay of 21,299 greedy Qwen2.5-1.5B requests with 5.1M output tokens (UltraChat, Alpaca, GSM8K, Spec-Bench, code edit, rewrite and templated JSON), in waves of 64, with a 1M-token corpus and k=8. Mean tokens per step. Arctic runs via `arctic_inference` and also sees responses still being generated. The kernel matches the replay on all 1,280 sampled drafts. | Drafter | All | Code edit | Rewrite | Templated JSON | |---|---|---|---|---| | Own history only | 1.651 | 5.50 | 4.74 | 1.65 | | **This PR** | **1.937** | 5.45 | 4.69 | 4.25 | | Exact corpus search + same vote (upper bound) | 1.956 | 5.45 | 4.69 | 4.28 | | Arctic (V1), k=8 | 1.923 | 5.12 | 4.07 | 3.89 | | Arctic (V1), k=24 | 1.948 | 5.89 | 4.37 | 4.11 | **Throughput.** Offline `LLM.generate` on this PR's final code. Output tokens/s relative to no speculation. - **Setup:** concurrency = `max_num_seqs`; prompts from a pinned pool with the replay's category mix (its GSM8K and Spec-Bench prompts also appear in the replay); greedy, `max_tokens=256`, k=8. - **Backends:** FlashAttention 2, except adaptive verification on `TRITON_ATTN`, which is compared against no speculation on `TRITON_ATTN`. - **Runs:** one per point; runs with another process on the GPU were discarded and rerun. | Model | Concurrency | `ngram_gpu` | Arctic (V1) | This PR | This PR + adaptive verification | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Qwen2.5-7B | 1 / 8 / 32 / 64 | 1.28 / 1.14 / 0.73 / 0.52x | 1.31 / 1.29 / 1.24 / 1.03x | 1.46 / 1.32 / 0.82 / 0.59x | **1.39 / 1.36 / 1.24 / 1.18x** | | Qwen2.5-1.5B | 1 / 8 / 32 / 64 / 128 / 256 | 1.45 / 1.25 / 0.84 / 0.55 / 0.50 / 0.44x | 1.41 / 1.43 / 1.17 / 1.00 / 0.91 / 0.82x | 1.66 / 1.47 / 0.97 / 0.64 / 0.56 / 0.52x | **1.56 / 1.29 / 1.15 / 1.05 / 0.99 / 0.91x** | - **Where Arctic wins:** 1.5B at concurrency 8 and 32, by 11% and 5% in absolute tok/s. Adaptive verification trims too much there (open question 2). - **Backend difference:** at 1.5B concurrency 128 / 256, `TRITON_ATTN` without speculation is 1.13 / 1.21x faster than FA2. Against the FA2 baseline the other columns use, adaptive verification is 1.12 / 1.10x. - **With #61509:** the 7B KV cache with adaptive verification grows from 21–46K to 50–70K tokens. 7B throughput becomes 1.38 / 1.32 / 1.30 / 1.15x, within run-to-run noise except at concurrency 32. **Online serving** (`vllm bench serve`, Qwen2.5-7B, prompts not in the 256-request warm-up, up to 256 output tokens, `--generation-config vllm`). Output throughput vs no speculation: | Config | Concurrency 1 / 8 / 32 / 64 | |---|---| | `ngram_gpu` | 1.26 / 1.11 / 0.73 / 0.53x | | Arctic (V1) | 1.42 / 1.37 / 1.24 / 1.10x | | This PR | 1.49 / 1.35 / 0.87 / 0.65x | | **This PR + adaptive verification** (vs no-spec on `TRITON_ATTN`) | **1.44 / 1.44 / 1.30 / 1.23x** | Median TTFT at concurrency 1 is 125 ms with this PR (with or without adaptive verification) and with `ngram_gpu`, vs 73 ms without speculation and 74 ms for Arctic on V1, which runs without async scheduling. That is about one decode step, so it's a V2 spec-decode cost rather than a suffix one.
GSM8K, workloads and correctness checks **GSM8K** (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, all 1,319 questions, 5-shot, `max_num_seqs=128`). Accuracy matches within noise (binomial SE about 1 point); at this load speculation doesn't speed it up: | Config | Greedy | Temperature 0.7 | Wall time (greedy) | |---|---|---|---| | No speculation (FA2) | 83.0% | 81.7% | 193 s | | No speculation (`TRITON_ATTN`) | 83.4% | 82.3% | 156 s | | Arctic (V1) | 83.4% | 83.2% | 252 s | | This PR | 82.8% | 83.6% | 387 s | | This PR + adaptive verification (`TRITON_ATTN`) | 82.9% | 81.6% | 157 s | **Workloads.** Offline, throughput vs no speculation (adaptive verification vs no-spec on `TRITON_ATTN`). Concurrency 32, except long context: | Workload | This PR | + adaptive verification | Arctic (V1) | |---|---|---|---| | VLM: Qwen2.5-VL-3B, 360 distinct camera frames, templated JSON reports and captions | 1.38x (3.18 tok/step) | 1.50x | 1.56x | | RL rollouts: Qwen2.5-1.5B, GSM8K, n=8, temperature 1 | 0.94x | 1.40x | 1.16x | | Multi-turn chat: Qwen2.5-7B, UltraChat history | 0.78x | 1.15x | 1.03x | | RAG + summarization: Qwen2.5-7B, Spec-Bench | 0.86x | 1.16x | 1.10x | | Long-context decode: 24K-token prompts, concurrency 3 | 1.38x | 0.29x; **1.46x with #61509** | 1.19x | At long context, adaptive verification's startup profiling cost the KV cache 1.9 GiB (43K instead of 80K tokens), so prefixes were evicted and re-prefilled. #61509 fixes that accounting on main. **Correctness** (this PR's final code; greedy outputs vs no speculation, 48 distinct prompts; fp32 Qwen2.5-0.5B on `TRITON_ATTN`, since FA2 has no fp32): | Check | This PR | + adaptive verification | `ngram_gpu` | |---|---|---|---| | Plain greedy | 45/48 | 45/48 | 46/48 | | Repetition/frequency/presence penalties | 43/48 | 44/48 | 43/48 | | Structured outputs (JSON schema, regex, choice), `max_tokens=2`, logprobs | identical | identical | regex 11/12, rest identical | | Stop strings with `min_tokens`; `ignore_eos` to 300 tokens | 48/48; 45/48 | 47/48; 45/48 | 47/48; 45/48 | | 24 distinct 800–1,800-word prompts with chunked prefill (`max_num_batched_tokens=512`); 8 prompts ending 40 tokens before `max_model_len` | 24/24, 8/8 | 24/24, 8/8 | 24/24, 8/8 | | Preemption (small KV cache, 144 requests, 355–509 preemptions) | 128/144 | 125/144 | 126/144 | - **Baseline noise:** two no-spec runs, async vs sync scheduling, differ on 1/48 plain prompts. - **Logprobs:** deltas on identical outputs are at most 5e-3, the same as `ngram_gpu`. - **Sampling** (Qwen2.5-1.5B bf16, temperature 1, top-p, top-k, n=16, each method with its own seed): total-variation distance of per-position token marginals vs a no-spec run is 0.153 / 0.079 / 0.131. A second no-spec run gives 0.161 / 0.059 / 0.128, `ngram_gpu` 0.148 / 0.056 / 0.131. - **Aborts** (`vllm serve`, 48 streams aborted mid-generation): the server stays healthy. Greedy requests sent afterwards match those sent before 8/8 without adaptive verification. With it, 7/8 in fp32 (one flip at a 0.0004-nat near-tie) and 2/8 in bf16 7B: the number of verified slots changes the batch shapes.
## Details **How it works** - **Own history:** the longest suffix match within the request's prompt and output, up to `suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth`. Same kernel layout as `ngram_gpu`. - **Cross-request corpus:** finished responses go into a GPU token ring (`suffix_decoding_corpus_tokens`, default 1M). A hash index on each request's last 2 and last 4 tokens returns up to 16 candidate positions. Each is verified and extended to its full suffix match, so the index is only an entry point for suffix matching, and hash collisions or overwritten documents only cost a candidate. - **Frequency vote:** for each candidate match length, the candidates matching at least that long vote on the continuation, as in SuffixDecoding. The highest-scoring chain wins, ties going to the longer match; then the longer of the own-history and corpus matches wins. - **Adaptive verification** (`enable_adaptive_verification`): per-slot confidences, learned online by source, match length and position, let the runner trim slots that aren't worth verifying. - **Ingestion:** one GPU program per (document, block). Each program replays the batch's placement to find its offset and skips positions that a later document of the same batch overwrites. Every position is written by exactly one program, so the result is exact and order-independent even when a burst is larger than the ring. A 256 × 4,096-token burst at the default 1M ring takes 0.58 ms. - **TP consistency without collectives:** finished ids are ingested in sorted order, index inserts use `atomic_max` over `(document << 32 | position)`, and the statistics are integer counters. - **Memory at the defaults:** 36 MB (4 MB corpus plus a 32 MB index). Suffix decoding also keeps the runner's token history on the GPU (`max_num_seqs × max_model_len × 4` bytes, e.g. 32 MiB at 256 × 32K).
How a corpus lookup works (diagram) ``` Request history: ... "report" "the" "camera" "at" "the" "north" "gate" └──── last 4 ────┘ └─ last 2 ┘ 1) LOOK UP hash(last 4), hash(last 2) -> buckets, 8 slots each (slot = newest occurrence in each of the last 8 documents) 2) EXTEND BACKWARDS each candidate against the request (up to 24 tokens): request: report the camera at the north gate corpus: log: the camera at the north gate -> match length 6 stale or colliding candidate -> length 0, dropped 3) VOTE + DRAFT candidates matching >= L tokens vote on the next k tokens; the chain with the highest summed probability wins 4) COMPARE with the longest match in the request's own history; the longer match wins, empty slots get the last token ``` Ingestion when a request finishes: `[last 3 prompt tokens | response]` is appended to the ring, and each position with at least 2 (4) tokens before it in the document is indexed under them: `table[hash][doc % 8] = max(existing, (doc, pos))`.
**Why a hash index** | Index | Propose cost (L4) | Notes | |---|---|---| | Suffix tree (Arctic, V1) | CPU, per request | Host sync, so no MRV2 or async scheduling | | Suffix array (#52097) | 1.3–4.5 ms as an eager library call (prototype measurement on a shared L4); #52097 reports 0.4–1.9 ms with its CUDA-graph path (L20, k=16) | Background rebuilds, epochs and a CPU collective for TP | | Brute-force GPU scan | 0.3–1.2 ms at batch 128 (prototype measurement) | Exact; cost grows with batch × corpus | | **Hash index + vote (this PR)** | **11–35 µs** GPU time for batch 1–256 (CUDA-graph microbenchmark), the same at 1M and 4M corpus tokens. As the engine runs it (eagerly): 89–95 µs per step at 4K context for batch 1–256, 231 µs at 128K context with 32 requests (`ngram_gpu`: 75–78 and 111 µs) | No rebuilds. The index alone is within 0.4% of an exact longest-match search; with the vote, about 1% below exact search + vote | One difference from Arctic: corpus matches need at least 2 tokens (so `suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth` must be at least 2 for the corpus), while own-history matches can be 1. Storing the last 3 prompt tokens with each response lets a response's first tokens be drafted from the corpus. **Taken from #52097 and @zip95297's MRV2 port** (`zip95297/vllm-dev`, branch `zip95297/suffix-gpu-mrv2`): GPU cross-request matching with no host sync; an `on_requests_finished` hook in `finish_requests` that ingests from `RequestState` and skips preempted requests (from the MRV2 port); sorting finished ids for TP consistency; the replay-based acceptance evaluation. **Changes outside the speculator** - `SuffixSpeculatorConfig` (`suffix/config.py`): suffix's default `num_speculative_tokens` is `min(8, suffix_decoding_max_tree_depth)` on both runners. On V1 it caps Arctic's dynamic draft length; set 24 for the previous V1 behavior. - `BaseSpeculator`: new no-op `add_request`, `on_requests_finished` and `reset_state` methods, which the runner and MRV2's kernel warmup call directly. The suffix speculator uses them to reset per-slot stats, ingest finished requests, and drop the warmup requests from the corpus. Dense `all_token_ids` for suffix. **Limitations** - Seeded sampling isn't reproducible with suffix decoding: drafts come from previously finished requests, and with adaptive verification the number of verified slots depends on the batch. The same seeded request sent alone twice gave identical output 0/4 (fp32; 4/4 without speculation). With `suffix_decoding_corpus_tokens: 0` and adaptive verification off it's 4/4. - The corpus is shared across requests regardless of `cache_salt` or LoRA adapter, like Arctic's global tree on V1 (documented; set `suffix_decoding_corpus_tokens: 0` to isolate). - Adaptive verification needs full CUDA graphs and an attention backend that replays variable-length decode batches. On L4 that is `TRITON_ATTN`: vLLM's FA2 backend declares uniform-batch support only. Until #61509 lands, its startup profiling also costs KV capacity, which matters at long context. - Under async scheduling a finished request can carry up to about 2k+1 tokens past the stop point into the corpus. ## Open questions 1. **Adaptive verification by default?** It is what makes suffix decoding pay off from concurrency 32 up. It isn't on by default here because it fails at startup on backends that can't replay variable-length decode graphs (FA2, the pre-Hopper default), so a default needs a fallback to off. Happy to add that here, or in a follow-up. 2. **Low-concurrency trimming.** Adaptive verification trims too much at low concurrency on small models: Qwen2.5-1.5B at concurrency 8 is 1.29x with it vs 1.47x verifying every slot (7B: 1.36x vs 1.32x). Tune it here (for example with a more optimistic prior) or later? 3. **Corpus default.** 4M tokens adds about 2–3% acceptance, but the index grows from 32 MB to 128 MB. 4. **Tokens past the stop point.** Pass the scheduler's final length down to ingestion? 5. **Arctic-only options** (`max_spec_factor`, `min_token_prob`) are ignored on V2 (documented). Warn as well? ## Follow-ups - Exclude filler slots from spec-decode metrics for GPU drafters (as #52097 does on V1 and its MRV2 branch does; see also #44056 and #50518). With adaptive verification, trimmed slots are still counted as drafted. - Index responses while they're still being generated. That may be why Arctic is ahead on the templated VLM workload. - CUDA-graph the propose path (@zip95297's bucketized draft graphs). - aarch64 benchmarks. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
**Not duplicating existing work:** the only other suffix decoding drafter PR is #52097 (`suffix_gpu` on V1), whose author is collaborating here; searches for "suffix decoding", "suffix_gpu" and "SuffixSpeculator" find no other MRV2 implementation. AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate, prototype, write and test this change. cc @njhill @zip95297 @benchislett @TheEpicDolphin

commits.pr_title: [Mooncake] Support selective leases for prefix lookups
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`MooncakeStoreConnector` prefix lookups call `batch_is_exist`, which grants a read lease on every key it finds and moves it to the hot end of the eviction order. A lookup therefore renews every stored key of the prompt, including keys that loading the hit never reads: blocks outside a sliding window, or the per-block-boundary states of linear-attention / Mamba layers before the hit's tail. Once the store is full, those never-loaded keys look hot and survive eviction, while keys that later requests would actually load are evicted.

This PR adds an opt-in mode, `VLLM_MOONCAKE_STORE_SELECTIVE_LEASE=1`, in which a lookup:

1. probes the candidate keys with `batch_probe_key`, which checks existence without leasing ([kvcache-ai/Mooncake#3801](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/3801));
2. computes the hit as before;
3. leases only the keys that loading that hit reads (`batch_is_exist` on the hit's load set, per group load mask and tail key).

If a key was evicted between the probe and the lease, the hit gets shorter, and the shorter hit can end at a key the first lease did not cover (for example, an earlier boundary state). So the shorter hit is leased in a second round. A hit is returned only when the lease on all of its keys succeeded; otherwise the lookup reports a miss. A failing lease RPC also reports a miss and never breaks the lookup server.

The default path is unchanged.

## Changes

- New `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/selective_lease.py`: `SelectiveLookupLease` (probe, compute the load set, lease, record the `lookup_lease` operation in the connector metrics).
- `store/worker.py`: when the env var is set, the lookup probes through `SelectiveLookupLease` and passes its hit to `lease_hit`. The longest-hit computation moves into `_longest_hit` so it can be reused after an eviction.
- `envs.py`: `VLLM_MOONCAKE_STORE_SELECTIVE_LEASE` (default off).
- Startup fails with a clear error if the installed Mooncake lacks `MooncakeDistributedStore.batch_probe_key`.

## Requirements

Requires Mooncake >= 0.3.14 on the master and every client. `batch_probe_key` is not in a tagged release yet; this was tested with the nightly `0.3.14.dev20261022`.

## Test Plan

Unit tests in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_hma_e2e.py`, on a full-attention + Mamba (align mode) worker over an in-memory store:

- default mode still leases every probed key;
- selective mode leases only the loaded keys, and they cover every key the load reads (including partial hash hits);
- a key evicted between probe and lease yields a shorter, fully leased hit; continued evictions yield no hit;
- error results and a raising lease RPC report a miss;
- startup fails without `batch_probe_key`.

End-to-end A/B on Kimi-K3 (hybrid KDA + MLA), disaggregated 4 prefill workers (TP8) + 1 decode worker (DEP16) on GB300, agentic coding traces at concurrency 480, 60 min. Mooncake store with 160 GB per rank (7.5 TB total), eviction at 95% high-watermark. Both arms run the same build and the same Mooncake nightly; only the env var differs.

## Test Result

### Disaggregated, 4P1D (DEP16 decode), concurrency 480

| metric | lease all (default) | selective lease | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| total throughput / GPU (tok/s) | 27,491 | 28,305 | +3.0% |
| P90 ITL | 35.8 ms | 36.4 ms | +1.7% |
| TTFT P50 | 2.35 s | 1.73 s | −26% |
| TTFT P90 | 12.8 s | 3.83 s | −70% |
| TTFT P95 | 20.9 s | 6.39 s | −69% |
| E2E latency P90 | 79.0 s | 75.8 s | −4% |
| prefix cache hit rate (benchmark) | 93.4% | 95.0% | +1.6 pt |

The store's raw capacity is the same in both arms: about 523k keys at the watermark, 10% evicted per pass, no failed evictions. What changes is which keys survive. A per-request audit against the trace (which prefixes had a saved state available when the request arrived) shows misses on states saved 2–10 min earlier falling from 1.13 to 0.21 points of prompt tokens, and on states older than 10 min from 1.55 to 0.91. Misses on states younger than 2 min are unchanged (0.46 vs 0.45), since nothing that young is evicted.

Cost: the extra lease RPC averages 1.07 ms (P90 1.9 ms) per lookup, with no errors and no keys evicted between probe and lease during the run. The lease-free probe was itself slightly faster than the leasing one (36.8 ms vs 43.1 ms average).

### Aggregated, concurrency sweep

One aggregated worker (TP8, DCP8, FP8 KV cache) on 8 GB300 GPUs, the same agentic coding traces, 60 min per run, Mooncake store with 160 GB per rank (1.25 TB total). Both arms run the same build; only the env var differs. Prefix cache hit rate is the benchmark's: cached prompt tokens / prompt tokens over the measured requests.

| concurrency | lease | prefix cache hit rate | throughput / GPU (tok/s) | TTFT P50 / P90 | P90 ITL | E2E latency P90 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 48 | all (default) | 96.50% | 19,921 | 1.13 / 2.58 s | 36.1 ms | 61.3 s |
| 48 | selective | 96.22% | 19,531 (−2.0%) | 1.10 / 2.81 s | 36.4 ms | 63.3 s |
| 64 | all (default) | 95.05% | 19,574 | 1.42 / 4.87 s | 55.9 ms | 94.6 s |
| 64 | selective | 95.18% | 20,341 (+3.9%) | 1.36 / 3.96 s | 52.6 ms | 84.8 s |
| 80 | all (default) | 93.33% | 18,104 | 6.09 / 21.2 s | 80.6 ms | 127.0 s |
| 80 | selective | 93.93% | 19,254 (+6.4%) | 5.30 / 19.4 s | 72.2 ms | 117.9 s |
| 96 | all (default) | 92.48% | 16,599 | 27.1 / 53.1 s | 84.8 ms | 156.9 s |
| 96 | selective | 93.97% | 18,080 (+8.9%) | 24.6 / 43.2 s | 73.5 ms | 145.9 s |

The gain grows with concurrency, i.e. with pressure on the store: at concurrency 96, misses on states that were saved and later evicted fall from 2.7 to 1.0 points of prompt tokens. Since the GPU KV cache is full from concurrency 64 on, the extra hits also save prefill work in the shared worker, which shows up as lower ITL.

At concurrency 48 the store is under little pressure, and selective lease is slightly worse. The difference comes from a few long requests (150k–690k tokens) that resumed from a state saved at an earlier boundary and not loaded since: the default mode kept it alive because later lookups over the same prefix renewed it, while selective lease let it age out. This is the trade-off of the mode: states that are only passed over by lookups are no longer protected.

---

commits.pr_title: [CI/Build] Add batch-invariance auto-label rule
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add auto-label rules for the new `batch-invariance` label, so that all batch-invariance and determinism work can be found with one filter. 

## Claims

- **PRs (mergify):** a PR gets the label if it changes a file whose path contains `batch_invariant`, `batch-invariant` or `determinism`. It also gets the label if its title names batch invariance or determinism.
- **Issues (keyword workflow):** an issue gets the label if its title names batch invariance or determinism. Bodies are not checked.
- **Title patterns:**
  - batch- or TP-invariance
  - an uppercase `BI` tag
  - determinism, non-deterministic, not reproducible or run-to-run
  - batch-dependent
  - "identical / same / repeated runs, requests or calls"
- **Bare "deterministic":** PRs only. Issue titles use it for crashes that always reproduce, such as "deterministic illegal address".

## Validation

I ran both rules against every open item on 2026-11-02: 2,758 issues and 7,045 PRs, with their file lists.
- **Mergify:** I copied the regexes out of the edited `mergify.yml` and ran them with Python `re`.
- **Issue workflow:** I ran the real `github-script` code from the edited workflow in Node, with stubbed `context`/`github` objects.

| | Matched | False positives | Related but missed |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Open PRs | 106 | 10 | 10 |
| Open issues | 41 | 3 | 14 |

- **How I checked for misses:** I compared the matches against 13 GitHub searches (these also search comments) and read every result the rules did not catch.
- **PR false positives:** large formatting or lint PRs that happen to touch the batch-invariance files, plus "deterministic suffix mapping" and "batch size dependency" in the title.
- **Missed issues:** they mention batch invariance only in the body.
- **Backfill:** I already applied the label by hand to the 158 related open items (`is:open label:batch-invariance`).

`pre-commit run --files .github/mergify.yml .github/workflows/issue_autolabel.yml` passes, including actionlint and "Check auto-label rules still match real files".

commits.pr_title: [Docs] List the Nemotron-3-Diarization plugin
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Lists NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Diarization (`Nemotron3DiarizationForAudioFrameClassification`, [`nvidia/Nemotron-3-Diarization`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3-Diarization)) as supported through the out-of-tree [vllm-nemotron-diarization-plugin](https://github.com/Alex-Wengg/vllm-nemotron-diarization-plugin).

## Why a plugin, not in-tree

#65002 added this model in-tree. @DarkLight1337 asked there:

> This is quite a small model. I wonder how much performance improvement does vLLM actually provide here over other baselines?

Not much: the model runs the Transformers forward once per recording, so offline throughput is close to calling Transformers directly. The value is convenience. Developers who already run vLLM can add speaker diarization with one `pip install`, through the same `LLM` API as their other models, without a separate NeMo setup. A plugin gives them that without vLLM carrying the model. He closed #65002 with:

> If you are ok with maintaining it and feel that it's valuable then you could do plugin. Either way let's close this PR.

So the model lives out of tree, and I maintain the plugin.

## Claims

- One row in the plugin table in `supported_models.md`.
- No vLLM code changes.

## Validation

The plugin on CPU with the V1 model runner, fp32, against Transformers `Nemotron3DiarizationForAudioFrameClassification` (two vLLM audio assets resampled to 16 kHz):

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Logits vs Transformers (2542 and 1595 frames) | max \|Δ\| ~2e-5, identical speaker segments |
| Batched vs single requests | identical |
| Prompt without audio | no frames, no crash |

## Details

- The plugin carries #65002's model, processor and config hooks without its core changes. Model Runner V2 has no path for raw-input-only models, so the plugin's `ModelState` hands each request's audio features to the model, as the V1 runner does natively. A prompt without audio returns no frames instead of being rejected in `input_processor.py`.
- No `_OOT_SUPPORTED_MODELS` entry, as with #65005: Transformers defines `Nemotron3DiarizationForAudioFrameClassification`, so without the plugin vLLM resolves it to the Transformers backend (`TransformersForCausalLM`) before it checks that table.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write the plugin and this PR. I reviewed the changed lines and ran the validation above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Pad extensible KV cache segments instead of rounding the block count
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #65204. Supersedes #65210 (carries over its connector gating, with Vegetog as co-author).

With the extensible KV cache (#56492), any KV connector made the engine round the KV block count down to a multiple of `granule / gcd(granule, block_stride)`. For awkward strides that multiple is huge, so engines with `--kv-offloading-size` could fail to start. This PR pads segment placement instead, and applies it (and the defragmenting commit) only for connectors that register the KV cache for RDMA.

## Claims

- `--kv-offloading-size` (and any connector that doesn't register the device KV cache) keeps its measured block count: no rounding, no padding, no defragmenting commit.
- NIXL / Mooncake / MoRIIO / UMBP keep one physical chunk per committed segment for RDMA registration at **any** block count, instead of losing up to one alignment unit (2048 blocks, ~11.6 GB, for the stride in #65204) or failing to start below it.
- `UMBPStoreConnector` is added to `registers_kv_cache_memory()`: it registers GPU KV storage through MORI. This also turns the extensible cache off for it on ROCm, as for MoRIIO.

## Validation

GB200, all on this branch unless noted.

**Reproducer**: `HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-360M-Instruct` (20 KiB page = 2¹²·5, so main needs a multiple of 512 blocks), `kv_offloading_size=1`, `block_size=16`, `max_model_len=1024`, `enforce_eager=True`. Baseline = `origin/main` versions of the changed files over the same build.

| `gpu_memory_utilization` | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 0.014 | fails at startup: "No available memory for the cache blocks … decrease `max_model_len`" (102 blocks rounded to 0) | starts, 102 blocks, correct greedy output |
| 0.018 | 1024 blocks | 1331 blocks, same output |

**NIXL P/D**: `tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/run_accuracy_test.sh` with `PREFILL_BLOCK_SIZE=16 DECODE_BLOCK_SIZE=16` (Qwen3-0.6B, 1P1D): passes for the default layer-outermost layout (padded) and with `--enable-cross-layers` (block-outermost, single segment), 0 failed transfers. A separate DEBUG run with `NixlConnector` confirmed the padded path ran: capacity 19254 blocks (main would have rounded to 19232), NIXL registered the padded segments, and the final 18624 blocks committed exactly the nominal 31.83 GiB.

**Unit tests**: `tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py`, `tests/utils_/test_extensible_tensor.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py`, `tests/v1/engine/test_engine_args.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py` all pass. New/changed coverage:
- `test_pad_kv_cache_segments` (CPU): uniform and mixed block strides, block-outermost no-op.
- `test_defragmenting_commit_backs_each_segment_with_one_allocation[padded]`: unpadded segments still share chunks after a defragmenting commit; padded ones get one chunk each at an unaligned count.
- `test_padded_config_allocates_and_defragments` (LBNHC, BLNHC, mixed strides): views, committed views and connector placements agree on a padded reservation.
- `test_extensible_extend_asks_connector_for_its_memory_pool`: a registering connector gets `defragment=True`.

## Details

**Root cause.** A connector that registers each committed segment for RDMA needs that segment backed by one physical chunk. Segments were placed at multiples of `capacity × block_stride`, so they only started on commit granules when the block count was a granule multiple; the engine forced that by rounding the reserved capacity and the post-warmup count for *every* connector. CPU offloading only copies blocks and needs none of it.

**Fix.**
- When `registers_kv_cache_memory()`, each worker pads its own copy of the KV cache config in `initialize_from_config` (`pad_kv_cache_segments`): each layer region of a block-compact layer-outermost layout starts on that device's commit granule. This costs address space only; commits already map whole granules per segment (`physical_bytes_for`), so a defragmenting commit of any count backs each segment with exactly one chunk. Block-outermost layouts have one segment at offset 0 and are untouched. KV connectors with the extensible cache are already restricted to block-compact layouts.
- Padding is worker-local so the engine/scheduler configs keep unpadded placements: `shrink_kv_cache_configs` scales `size` by block count and scheduler-side connectors read `size // num_blocks`.
- `ExtensibleKVCache` takes the layout to derive one segment per layer region (gaps allowed) rather than inferring segments from a single stride, which can't tell padding from LHBNC head groups for small caches.
- Removed: engine-side `align_extensible_kv_cache_capacity` / `granule_aligned_kv_cache_blocks`, the `kv_cache_commit_granule` RPC, `granule_aligned_blocks` / `granule_block_alignment`, `blocks_within(aligned=)`.
- The defragmenting commit is gated on `registers_kv_cache_memory()` (#65210).

**Tradeoff/limitation.** `registers_kv_cache_memory()` is a name-based allowlist, so out-of-tree connectors loaded via `kv_connector_module_path` that register device memory no longer get one-chunk segments by default (previously any connector did). Unpadded configs (no registering connector) behave as before.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MRV2][Spec Decode] Keep P/D prompt tails on FULL graphs with adaptive verification
commits.pr_body:
## Overview On a P/D decode instance with adaptive verification (AV), a step that admits a KV-transferred request runs eager instead of replaying the FULL decode graph, and under DP every rank runs eager with it. This PR fixes the condition that rejects the graph, in the runner and in the EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP drafter: two lines. ## Claims - **Before.** On D, a transferred request recomputes its last prompt token, so it is scheduled as 1 real token + K placeholder drafts, the shape of a decode row. It still counts as prefilling (`has_prefill=True`). The AV path (#57263) drops the query-length bound for any batch with `has_prefill`, so the AV decode graph rejects the step. The step runs eager under `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` (PIECEWISE under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`), and the requests already decoding in the batch run eager with it. DP ranks agree on the bound, so one rank's arrival makes every rank run eager. - **After.** The bound is dropped only when the batch is not `decode_graph_eligible` (#58400). That existing classifier admits a one-token extension over existing KV and rejects real prefills, and the non-AV decode path already uses it. The drafter uses the same condition, so it keeps the target's padded layout (#62796). - **Effect.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark, vLLM P/D recipe settings at 1P1D DEP4. On main, eager steps (about 6x slower than FULL) take 60–77% of D's time, and most of them are ranks pulled eager by another rank's arrival. With this PR all of them replay FULL: output throughput is **2.0x** (OSL 256) and **1.76x** (OSL 1024), and D TPOT goes from 19.2 to 6.95 ms and from 10.6 to 5.69 ms. - **No degradation expected.** The changed value only feeds CUDA graph dispatch, and matching is monotonic: a bound where there was `None` can only add a match, since graphs without a bound match either way. Only AV captures bounded graphs, so dispatch without AV is unchanged. Real prefills (multi-token prompts, one-token prompts without prior KV, PCP batches) still run eager or PIECEWISE. GSM8K and draft acceptance stay within the baseline's run-to-run spread (DSpark and MTP, TP4 and DEP4). - **No extra resources.** No new graphs are captured, so graph count, CUDA graph memory and KV cache size are unchanged. The condition is a host-side bool already computed each step, so there is no new GPU sync or DP collective. - **Trade-offs.** An arrival step now pads its requests to the graph's capture size, the same padding every decode step pays; it is still about 6x faster than eager in the runs below. With D under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, arrival steps move from PIECEWISE to FULL; D TPOT is unchanged within noise (TP4 cross-check below).
Code path on main: why an arrival step runs eager 1. **The arriving request counts as prefilling.** `prefill_len` is the number of tokens handed to the runner ([`states.py#L106`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/states.py#L106)), usually the prompt length. `num_computed_prefill_tokens = min(num_computed_tokens, prefill_len)` ([`model_runner.py#L1332-L1336`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L1332-L1336)). On D, the transferred KV covers all but the last prompt token, so the request arrives with `num_computed = prefill_len - 1` and is prefilling ([`#L1385-L1386`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L1385-L1386)). After that step `num_computed >= prefill_len`, and the request decodes. 2. **`has_prefill` clears the bound.** The runner passes `max_query_len = None` for any batch with `has_prefill` ([`model_runner.py#L1848-L1851`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L1848-L1851)), and so does the drafter ([`speculator.py#L273`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/target_dependent_ar/speculator.py#L273)). 3. **DP spreads `None`.** Ranks exchange the bound and keep it only if no rank sent `None` ([`dp_utils.py#L117-L119`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/dp_utils.py#L117-L119)). 4. **AV decode graphs need a bound.** With AV, decode graphs are captured as varlen graphs with `max_query_len=decode_query_len` ([`cudagraph_utils.py#L305-L319`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py#L305-L319)). A bounded graph matches only a batch that carries a bound within it ([`cudagraph_utils.py#L130-L133`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py#L130-L133)), so a `None` batch matches no decode graph. Under `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` there is no PIECEWISE graph to fall back to, so the step runs eager. 5. **Without AV this does not happen.** Uniform decode graphs carry no bound and are matched by `uniform_token_count`, which already uses `decode_graph_eligible` ([`model_runner.py#L1404`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L1404), [`utils.py#L1011`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/utils.py#L1011)). An arrival row (1 real token + K placeholder drafts) is uniform with the decode rows, so the step replays FULL. This PR uses `decode_graph_eligible` in step 2, the same classifier step 5 already uses.
## Validation All runs use upstream main `b8c04dd3b4` with that commit's precompiled wheel, 1P1D on two GB200 nodes over NIXL, with a fresh P/D pair per run. "Baseline" is that main commit without this PR. ### Performance The deployment follows the vLLM recipe preset for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D (`gb300_agentx_pd`, from InferenceX #3941), scaled to one GB200 node per role: - P: DEP4, 64 seqs/rank, `max_num_batched_tokens=32768`, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, no AV. - D: DEP4, 40 seqs/rank, `max_num_batched_tokens=400`, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` with capture sizes 6..240, AV on, no prefix caching. - Both: DSpark K=5, MegaAttention, MegaMoE, DeepSelect top-k, Engram CPU offload. The client keeps 320 requests in flight (2x D capacity). Each request goes to P with `max_tokens=1`, then streams from D. Prompts are unique, outputs use `ignore_eos`, and 640 warmup requests run first. Baseline and this PR run in ABAB order; the table shows both rounds. TPOT and TTFT are measured on the D stream; TTFT includes queueing, since the client oversubscribes D. | Workload | Version | Output tok/s | TPOT mean | TPOT p99 | D TTFT | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | ISL ~290, OSL 256, 4096 req | baseline | 4,100 / 4,385 | 19.0 / 19.4 ms | 33.4 / 32.8 ms | 7.4 / 6.8 s | | | this PR | **8,559 / 8,519** | **6.93 / 6.97 ms** | 10.5 / 10.5 ms | 3.6 / 3.7 s | | ISL ~2.2K, OSL 1024, 2048 req | baseline | 8,533 / 8,666 | 10.7 / 10.6 ms | 19.3 / 19.4 ms | 13.0 / 12.8 s | | | this PR | **15,099 / 15,231** | **5.71 / 5.66 ms** | 9.9 / 10.1 ms | 7.3 / 7.2 s | **Why it is large under data parallelism.** DP ranks agree on one graph shape per step, and the agreed query-length bound is `None` if any rank sends `None`. So a single rank admitting a transferred request forces every rank's step to run eager, including ranks that only have decodes. A second traced run of the same setup splits D's steps per rank (4 ranks, warmup excluded). Step time is the gap to the next step on the same rank: | Workload | Version | Own arrival steps | Decode steps forced eager by another rank | FULL decode steps | Time in eager steps | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | OSL 256 | baseline | 11.7%, eager, 102 ms | **20.5%, 102 ms** | 67.8%, 15.0 ms | 77% | | | this PR | 10.0%, FULL, 15.2 ms | 0 | 90.0%, 15.4 ms | 0 | | OSL 1024 | baseline | 5.4%, eager, 101 ms | **13.0%, 101 ms** | 81.6%, 17.1 ms | 60% | | | this PR | 5.5%, FULL, 16.1 ms | 0 | 94.5%, 17.7 ms | 0 | Steps forced eager by another rank outnumber a rank's own arrival steps 1.75–2.4x. The chance that some rank admits a request in a given step rises with the DP size, so we expect the effect to be larger on the recipe's DEP16 decode (not measured here). The gain depends on how often a decode step admits a transferred request, so it is smaller for longer outputs. In the TP4 cross-check below, D under `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` with this PR reaches the same TPOT (6.7 ms) as the same D under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, where arrival steps ran PIECEWISE instead of eager.
TP4 cross-check: P PIECEWISE, D TP4 FULL_DECODE_ONLY + AV, 128 seqs, 128 in flight, ISL ~290, OSL 256, 3 ABAB rounds | Model | Version | TPOT mean (3 rounds) | TPOT p99 | D TTFT | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark K=3 | baseline | 17.8 / 20.0 / 20.0 ms | 29.9-31.0 ms | 1.08-1.12 s | | | this PR | 6.72 / 6.70 / 6.75 ms | 9.4 ms | 0.40-0.42 s | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash + MTP K=3 | baseline | 17.8 / 24.7 / 25.8 ms | 35.0-37.6 ms | 1.41-1.54 s | | | this PR | 5.42 / 5.41 / 5.38 ms | 7.1-7.2 ms | 0.37-0.39 s | Same workload with D under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, where main runs arrival steps PIECEWISE and this PR runs them FULL: | Model | Version | TPOT mean | TPOT p99 | D TTFT | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark K=3 | baseline | 6.72 ms | 9.38 ms | 0.44 s | | | this PR | 6.75 ms | 9.27 ms | 0.41 s | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash + MTP K=3 | baseline | 5.44 / 5.68 ms | 7.41 / 7.48 ms | 0.47 / 0.39 s | | | this PR | 5.33 ms | 7.19 ms | 0.39 s |
### Correctness Setup: - P and D TP4 + EP. - D: `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` + AV, 128 seqs. - The decode-side graph mode is traced per step on all ranks; the ranks agree. - "Arrival step" means a decode-eligible batch with `has_prefill`, i.e. it contains a transferred request computing its last prompt token. Workload per run: - 8 serial prompts (19..8195 tokens), 16 staggered and 32 burst requests. - Two direct-to-D negative controls: a multi-token prompt without transferred KV, and a fresh one-token prompt. - Full GSM8K: 1319 questions, 5-shot, concurrency 8, temperature 0. **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark (K=3)** | Version | Arrival steps | Real prefills | GSM8K | Accepted tokens / draft | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | baseline | 1128 eager | 6 eager | 1190 / 1319 | 1.962 | | this PR | **1316 FULL** | 6 eager | 1194 / 1319 | 1.961 | | baseline, repeat | | | 1187 / 1319 | 1.976 | **DeepSeek-V4-Flash + MTP (K=3)**, which uses `TargetDependentARSpeculator` | Version | Arrival steps: target / drafter | GSM8K | Accepted tokens / draft | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | baseline | eager / eager (1010) | 1248 / 1319 | 1.879 | | runner condition only | FULL / **eager** (1168) | 1249 / 1319 | 1.877 | | this PR | **FULL / FULL** (1163) | 1253 / 1319 | 1.873 | **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark (K=5), DEP4 recipe config from the performance section** | Version | Own arrival steps | Decode steps forced eager by another rank | Real prefills | GSM8K | Accepted tokens / draft | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | baseline | 5.0%, eager | 11.7%, eager | 2 eager | 1193 / 1319 | 2.067 | | this PR | 5.1%, **FULL** | **0** | 2 eager | 1184 / 1319 | 2.049 | | baseline, repeat | | | | 1196 / 1319 | 2.048 | | this PR, repeat | | | | 1200 / 1319 | 2.090 | Serving with expert parallelism is not bitwise deterministic run to run. Baseline spans 1193–1196 and 2.048–2.067; this PR spans 1184–1200 and 2.049–2.090. Between the first baseline and first PR runs, 45 questions flip correct → wrong and 36 wrong → correct. With only the runner condition, an arrival step replays the target graph padded to, for example, 32 requests, while the drafter runs eager over the 7 real ones on the same attention metadata. That is the mismatch #62796 removed. On this sparse-MLA model it costs no measurable acceptance; #62793 shows that it does on FA3. In every run, all measured requests succeeded, with no preemptions and no KV transfer failures. Pure decode steps are FULL in every run, except the startup warmup steps, which run eager. The GSM8K and acceptance differences fall within the baseline repeat spread.
Unit tests ```bash pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_dp_utils.py \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py # 116 passed, on the branch rebased onto current main ``` - Reverting only the runner condition fails `test_prompt_tail_keeps_decode_graph_bound[True-8]`. - Reverting only the drafter condition fails `test_draft_prefill_matches_shared_target_metadata_shape[decode-eligible-prefill-tail]`. - Both files already run in CI under `tests/v1/worker` and `tests/v1/cudagraph`.
## Details **Request path.** 1. The proxy sends the prompt to P with `max_tokens=1` and `do_remote_decode`; P prefills and returns KV transfer metadata. 2. The proxy sends the same prompt with that metadata to D. D's scheduler pulls the KV over NIXL and marks the whole prompt as computed. 3. On load completion, the scheduler sets `num_computed_tokens = N - 1`, so D recomputes the last prompt position to get logits for its first sampled token. With K speculative tokens, the request is scheduled as 1 real token + K placeholder drafts (`q = K + 1`): the shape of a decode row. 4. The runner classifies the batch and dispatches a CUDA graph. This step is the one that changes. **Root cause.** In step 4, the request is still prefilling (`num_computed_prefill < prefill_len`), so `has_prefill` is True. - #57263 cleared the runner's `max_query_len` for any batch with `has_prefill`, because a varlen decode graph matched on that bound alone would admit a short real prefill. - Two days later, #58400 added `decode_graph_eligible`, which treats a one-token extension over existing context as a decode. Input preparation already handles this case through `prefill_runs_as_decode`. #58400 wired the classification into the uniform decode path only. - The varlen path that AV uses kept the `has_prefill` check. So with AV off, D replays FULL on arrival steps; with AV on, it does not. - `TargetDependentARSpeculator.propose` has the same check for its draft-prefill dispatch. **Dispatch before and after.** The red edge is main's path for a P/D arrival step; the green edge is the path this PR takes. Real prefills take the grey path in both. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["D step: transferred request = 1 real token + K placeholder drafts
(+ requests already decoding)"] --> B["gather_batch_req_state
has_prefill = True
decode_graph_eligible = True"] P["Real prefill: multi-token prompt, or one-token prompt without context"] --> Q["decode_graph_eligible = False"] Q --> N B -->|"main: if has_prefill"| N["max_query_len = None"] B -->|"this PR: if not decode_graph_eligible"| K["max_query_len = K + 1"] N --> S["DP sync: the agreed bound is None if any rank sent None"] S --> X["AV varlen FULL decode graph rejected on every DP rank
FULL_DECODE_ONLY → eager · FULL_AND_PIECEWISE → PIECEWISE"] K --> Y["AV varlen FULL decode graph replayed
(drafter draft-prefill uses the same bound and padded layout)"] linkStyle 3 stroke:#d62728,stroke-width:3px linkStyle 4 stroke:#2ca02c,stroke-width:3px linkStyle 2 stroke:#999999 ``` Without AV, the decode graph is matched by `uniform_token_count`, which already uses `decode_graph_eligible`, so arrival steps were not affected. **Change.** - Two conditions change from `has_prefill` to `not decode_graph_eligible`: one in `GPUModelRunner.execute_model`, one in `TargetDependentARSpeculator.propose`. The other edits update comments that described the old rule. - The classifier, scheduler, input preparation, capture sizes and kernels are unchanged. - Keeping the bound only removes one rejection reason. The existing graph checks (query-length bound, request/token coverage, explicit eager, DP agreement on the bound) still apply. - DFlash/DSpark drafters dispatch with a fixed uniform shape and are not affected. - Model Runner V1 does not support AV, so it needs no change. **Relation to #64915.** #64915 contains the same runner condition as part of a larger feature: varlen decode graphs for fixed-width speculation, with new backend and capacity checks. This PR is only the AV bug fix. It adds the drafter condition, which #64915 lacks, plus a regression test and P/D validation with real KV transfer, which #64915 lists as outstanding. If this PR merges first, #64915 drops the overlapping line. No other open PR changes these conditions. **Limitations.** - GPU validation covers DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DSpark) and DeepSeek-V4-Flash (MTP) on GB200 with the MLA backends those models use. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Gate FlashInfer all-reduce on 16-byte row widths
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

FlashInfer's fused all-reduce cannot run every tensor shape and [`should_use_fi_ar`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/ef5bcaa387632c9943f1e1cd0716354d75b99285/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/flashinfer_all_reduce.py#L469) checks all the kernel requirements. However, this is not complete as it never validated row width, so a tensor whose row is not a whole number of 16-byte vectors passed the gate and reached a kernel that cannot run it. On the MNNVL backend this kills the worker; on the trtllm backend, which has no equivalent assert, it truncates its indexing and silently returns wrong results. This PR adds the missing check so these reductions fall back to NCCL.

Mamba2 with `mamba_n_groups=1` hits this at TP>1 (see [`mamba_mixer2.py:144`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/87b804f09d698bdcc5dc53062d2058d7faad08ca/vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_mixer2.py#L144)). Since https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52998 made `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER` default to on, hybrid models using Mamba2 layers such as `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny` cannot start out of the box.

To reproduce on `main`:

```
vllm serve ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 1024 --trust-remote-code
```

fails to start on main (49dbf7c44f8157285db653fbe789daa30df6cfc4) with the following message:

```
(EngineCore pid=2676902) ERROR 10-20 09:35:05 [core.py:1545] RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'Check failed: token_dim % (sizeof(float4) / sizeof(c_type)) == 0 (1 vs. 0) : token_dim must be divisible by 4', please check the stack trace above for the root cause
(EngineCore pid=2676902) ERROR 10-20 09:35:09 [multiproc_executor.py:315] Worker proc VllmWorker-0 died unexpectedly (exit code: None), shutting down executor.
```

However, it starts correctly with the VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER disabled:

```
VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0 \
  vllm serve ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 1024 --trust-remote-code
```

CC: @njhill @tdoublep @jeejeelee 

## Claims

- Granite-4 (and any Mamba2 model with `n_groups == 1`) starts at TP>1 with the default FlashInfer all-reduce, instead of dying in `determine_available_memory`.
- Closes a silent-correctness hole on the trtllm backend, which vectorizes the same way but validates nothing.
- Pure gating change: shapes the kernel already accepted take exactly the same path as before. Only shapes that previously crashed now fall back.

## Validation

- **End-to-end.** On main, the serve command above does not start unless FlashInfer all-reduce is disabled:

```
VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0 \
  vllm serve ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 1024 --trust-remote-code
```

starts as expected. With this PR, the same command *without* the env var starts and serves.

Both the failure and the fix were exercised on the default `auto` backend, which resolves to mnnvl on this 8x H100 box. Similar results for a 2x GB200.

- **Unit test.** `tests/distributed/test_flashinfer_all_reduce.py` covers the shape/dtype combinations the gate has to separate:

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/test_flashinfer_all_reduce.py -v
```

| shape | dtype | row bytes | accepted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `(16, 1)` | fp32 | 4 | no |
| `(16, 2)` | fp32 | 8 | no |
| `(16, 1)` | bf16 | 2 | no |
| `(16, 4)` | bf16 | 8 | no |
| `(16, 4)` | fp32 | 16 | yes |
| `(16, 8)` | bf16 | 16 | yes |
| `(16, 4096)` | bf16 | 8192 | yes |

The change only diverts shapes that previously aborted the worker onto the NCCL path, which is the default reduction when the FlashInfer all-reduce is off. Shapes the kernel already accepted are unaffected, so there is no numerical delta to measure.

## Details

### Root cause

FlashInfer's fused all-reduce kernels load each token row as a `float4`, so a row must be a whole number of 16-byte vectors. The MNNVL kernel enforces this with a throwing TVM FFI `ICHECK` ([`trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce.cu:59-60`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/csrc/trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce.cu#L59-L60)):

```cpp
TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(token_dim % (sizeof(float4) / sizeof(c_type)), 0)
    << "token_dim must be divisible by " << sizeof(float4) / sizeof(c_type);
```

The divisor is dtype-dependent — 4 for fp32, 8 for fp16/bf16 — so the observed "token_dim must be divisible by 4" is the fp32 instantiation of the general rule, not a fixed bound. The trtllm path vectorizes the same way (`reinterpret_cast<float4*>` indexed as `hidden_dim / VEC_SIZE`) but carries no equivalent assert, so an undersized dim there truncates its indexing instead of aborting.

`should_use_fi_ar` validated device, rank, contiguity, dtype and workspace capacity, but never row width. A narrow tensor therefore passed the gate and the throwing assert killed the worker instead of the communicator falling back to NCCL.

Mamba2 with `mamba_n_groups=1` hits this at TP>1. The gated RMSNorm parallelizes over the reduction dim and all-reduces an fp32 `(num_tokens, 1)` partial sum ([`mamba_mixer2.py:143-144`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/49dbf7c44f8157285db653fbe789daa30df6cfc4/vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_mixer2.py#L143-L144)):

```python
local_sums = x.pow(2).sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
global_sums = tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(local_sums)
```

A row of one fp32 is 4 bytes, so the kernel rejects it and the engine dies inside `determine_available_memory`.

### Why nobody hit this earlier

Both halves predate the user-visible breakage:

| when | what | PR |
|---|---|---|
| 2025-02-22 | `n_groups == 1` TP all-reduce added to `Mixer2RMSNormGated` | #13660 |
| 2026-02-26 | `should_use_fi_ar` reaches current form, no row-width check | #34109 |
| 2026-08-20 | `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER` flipped `0` → `1` | #52998 |

The narrow shape and the unvalidated gate coexisted for ~6 months, reachable only by users who explicitly opted in. #52998 exposed the bug rather than creating it.

### Why gate, rather than fix the caller

A caller-side flatten in `mamba_mixer2.py` would be smaller, and there is precedent for it — see #44983 below. Two reasons to prefer the gate:

- **It is not Mamba2's bug.** Any caller reducing a narrow fp32 tensor hits the same kernel constraint. The gate's job is to decide which shapes the kernel can run, and it was answering that question incompletely.
- **The trtllm path needs it regardless.** A caller-side fix for Granite leaves these shapes silently corrupting results on the backend with no assert.

A `try`/`except` fallback would be worse than either: a rank that catches the assert and falls back while its peers proceed deadlocks the collective. The fix has to be a deterministic predicate that all ranks evaluate identically.

### Relation to MiniMax, #44983

MiniMax has a structurally identical reduction — a per-token fp32 variance all-reduced across TP inside an RMSNorm — and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44983 fixed it caller-side by flattening before the reduction ([`rms_norm_tp.py:41`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/49dbf7c44f8157285db653fbe789daa30df6cfc4/vllm/model_executor/layers/minimax_rms_norm/rms_norm_tp.py#L41)), relying on the `len(shape) != 2` check in `should_use_fi_ar` to keep 1-D inputs off the FlashInfer path.


## Not a duplicate

Checked per `AGENTS.md`:

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "flashinfer all reduce"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "should_use_fi_ar"
```

No open PR adds a row-alignment check, so this is not a duplicate. Three open PRs are nearby, and two touch the same file:

- **#55973** — fixes FlashInfer fused all-reduce when NVLink multicast is unavailable. Same file, but entirely inside `get_fi_ar_workspace` (it caches unsupported workspace configurations and bails out during CUDA graph capture).
  It does not touch `should_use_fi_ar`. Complementary rather than overlapping: it makes workspace *creation* failures survivable, this makes a *shape* the kernel rejects survivable.
- **#53852** — honours an explicit FlashInfer size override on H200. Same file, and it rewrites the `max_workspace_size` assignment in `__init__` immediately above this change. Textually adjacent, semantically independent (it decides *how big* the workspace is, this decides *which shapes* are eligible), but expect a trivial rebase if it merges first.
- **#60011** — makes `--disable-custom-all-reduce` fall back to NCCL. A different switch, does not touch this file, and does not address shapes the kernel rejects.

This PR was written with AI assistance (Claude); I reviewed every line.

---

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Skip custom-op dispatch for FlashInfer dense GEMMs in eager
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Cut the per-call host overhead vLLM adds in front of FlashInfer dense GEMMs (BF16, FP8 per-tensor and block-scale, MXFP8, NVFP4, W4A16) and their activation-quantize ops in eager mode, e.g. prefill without CUDA graphs. Companion to flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7788 (merged), which removed 25–50 µs from FlashInfer's own dispatch.

## Claims

- Eager host time per linear call drops by 31–53 µs (MXFP8 q_b 142 → 91 µs, NVFP4 q_b 130 → 97 µs; table below).
- The same bypass applies to the other FlashInfer GEMM ops: FP8 `bmm_fp8` and W4A16 `flashinfer_mm_bf16_fp4` save ~10–16 µs per call in an isolated op microbenchmark, and the quantize ops save 2–5 µs.
- Under `torch.compile`, the ops that were `torch.library.custom_op` now go through `direct_register_custom_op`, about 17–23 µs cheaper per call for the MXFP8 GEMM.
- No behavior change: op names, schemas and fake impls are unchanged, eager outputs are bit-identical, and compiled graphs still record the custom ops.

## Validation

Host µs per call (enqueue rate, warm, no per-call sync), FlashInfer cute-dsl backend (the SM100 default), Kimi K3 projection shapes (public config) at M=4096, FlashInfer with #7788. 15 interleaved rounds × 150 calls, medians; IQR ≤ 2 µs.

| path | shape (N×K) | bare FlashInfer call | vLLM `layer(x)` main | this PR | saved |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| MXFP8 | q_b 18432×1536 | 75.8 | 141.7 | **91.0** | 50.7 |
| MXFP8 | o_proj 7168×12288 | 69.7 | 136.8 | **85.4** | 51.4 |
| NVFP4 | q_b 18432×1536 | 63.3 | 130.3 | **97.3** | 33.0 |
| NVFP4 | o_proj 7168×12288 | 66.1 | 134.5 | **101.8** | 32.6 |

The cutlass backend shows the same savings (31–51 µs), and M=8 is within a few µs of M=4096.

- `torch.library.opcheck` (`test_schema`, `test_autograd_registration`, `test_faketensor`, `test_aot_dispatch_dynamic`) passes for `vllm::mm_mxfp8` and `vllm::flashinfer_mm_fp4` as re-registered, with `NvmlCudaPlatform` / dispatch key `CUDA`.
- Outputs of the eager path, the op path, and the direct FlashInfer call are bit-identical (`torch.equal`) for MXFP8 (cutlass, cute-dsl) and NVFP4 (cutlass, cute-dsl).
- `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` over the MXFP8 linear still records `vllm.mxfp8_quantize` and `vllm.mm_mxfp8` without graph breaks.

The second commit extends this to every FlashInfer dense-GEMM-path op. Isolated op microbenchmark, host µs per call (64×256×512), vLLM main → this PR. `opcheck`, eager == op (`torch.equal`), and `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` still emitting the op were checked for each:

| op | main (`custom_op`) | this PR (eager) |
|---|--:|--:|
| `mm_mxfp8` (cutlass) | 56.5 | 41.7 |
| `flashinfer_mm_fp4` (cutlass) | 58.0 | 43.7 |
| `bmm_fp8` (auto) | 58.2 | 42.6 |
| `flashinfer_mm_bf16_fp4` | n/a | 68.3 via op → 57.9 |
| `flashinfer_mxfp8_quantize_8x4` | 15.9 | 11.6 |
| `flashinfer_nvfp4_quantize` (8x4) | 22.4 | 17.2 |
| `flashinfer_mxfp4_quantize` | 18.2 | 13.4 |

Already directly registered, now also bypassed in eager (same checks; FP8 block-scale on H100 because the kernel is SM90; the `dynamic_` op was checked for eager == op and compile, not opcheck):

| op | via op | this PR (eager) |
|---|--:|--:|
| `cuda_flashinfer_bf16_gemm` (flashinfer_cutedsl) | 108.3 | 93.1 |
| `flashinfer_fp8_blockscale_gemm` (M=16, H100) | 20.1 | 17.3 |
| `dynamic_flashinfer_deepgemm_blockscale_gemm` (M=16, H100) | 23.7 | 20.0 |

**Limitations:** these numbers come from a harness that replicates the vLLM call path line by line (`ColumnParallelLinear.forward` / `RowParallelLinear.forward` → `ModelOptLinearMethod.apply` → the FlashInfer linear kernels in `kernels/linear/`), on an SM100 part. It is not an end-to-end serving benchmark. vLLM's compiled extension was not available in that environment, so for NVFP4 the C++ `scaled_fp4_quant` was substituted with an equivalent-schema op that launches FlashInfer's FP4 quantize kernel. Absolute NVFP4 numbers may therefore be high by up to ~13 µs, while the before/after delta is unaffected. Relying on CI for the existing tests, including `tests/kernels/quantization/test_flashinfer_mxfp8_trtllm.py`, which opchecks `vllm::mm_mxfp8`.

## Details

Root cause: `vllm::mm_mxfp8` and `vllm::flashinfer_mm_fp4` were registered with `@torch.library.custom_op`, the slow registration path that `direct_register_custom_op` exists to avoid. Every eager linear call went through them, plus `vllm::mxfp8_quantize`. A no-op with the same signature costs 8.3 µs as a `custom_op`, 3.2 µs via `direct_register_custom_op`, and 0.15 µs as a plain call. The real GEMM costs 32–35 µs more through the op than called directly, because FlashInfer's Python dispatch also runs slower under the dispatcher.

Changes:
- Add `eager_bypass_custom_op()` next to `direct_register_custom_op` in `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py`. It wraps a registered op so that only Dynamo tracing goes through the dispatcher, where the op is needed as a graph boundary; eager calls go straight to the implementation. `vllm/ir/op.py` uses the same idea for `enable_torch_wrap`.
- Move the FlashInfer `torch.library.custom_op` ops (`mm_mxfp8`, `flashinfer_mm_fp4`, `bmm_fp8`, `flashinfer_mm_bf16_fp4`, `flashinfer_mxfp4_quantize`, `flashinfer_nvfp4_quantize`, `flashinfer_mxfp8_quantize_8x4`) to `direct_register_custom_op`, keeping the same names, schemas and fake impls, and call them through the bypass. Do the same for the already directly-registered BF16 (`cuda_flashinfer_bf16_gemm`) and FP8 block-scale ops, and for `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize`.
- Cache the "use FlashInfer's MXFP8 quantize or fall back" decision (2 imports, a capability query and `has_flashinfer()` per call).

Not included, because these change semantics or are out of scope:
- `skip_check=True` on the FlashInfer GEMM, which would save a further 8–15 µs but drops FlashInfer's per-call validation.
- Folding quantize + GEMM into one op. That only helps compiled mode (~2–4 µs), and for NVFP4 it would hide `_C.scaled_fp4_quant` from the attention/quant fusion passes.
